text: open_layer_rows ( rows : tuple [ tuple [ RowItem , ... ], ... ], * , expected_id : int , master : str , deadline : float | None = None ) -> None Open exact glyph/layer occurrences in rows, in ONE verified fresh native tab. What: each row is a tuple of items. An item is (glyph name, exact layer name) , or SPACE ( (None, "") ) for one space. Rows are separated by one line break; an empty row keeps its line, as in open_named_tab . Use it for stacked or side-by-side layer comparisons (Master Text Comparison). How: the complete immutable request is validated first. Then every requested layer must exist in the font expected_id ( flPackage.id , the current font). Only then are native symbols built: a layer item is an fgSymbol with its own layerName ; a space is the text symbol list fgSymbolList(" ") and a line break fgSymbolList("\n") , the same text form that open_named_tab uses for line breaks. The tab opens through the shared fresh-tab fence ( _open_symbols ). master fences the current source master; it does not overwrite the layer of an item. Why: scripts must not build fgSymbol lists or call requestContent themselves. Any failure before the tab opens opens no tab. Native qualification (space text symbol, layer per symbol) remains open.
title: fontlabapp.proof.tabs.named.open_layer_rows

text: open_layer_tab ( layers : tuple [ tuple [ str , str ], ... ], * , expected_id : int , master : str , deadline : float | None = None ) -> None Open exact glyph/layer occurrences in a verified fresh native tab. Every pair is (glyph name, exact foreground layer name). Preserve auxiliary layers, mixed masters and repeated winners without Unicode/slash substitution. Validate the complete immutable request before native symbol allocation. The separate master argument fences the current source context; it does not overwrite each symbol's requested layer. Native qualification remains open.

text: open_named_tab ( lines : tuple [ tuple [ str , ... ], ... ], * , expected_id : int , master : str , deadline : float | None = None ) -> None Open a fresh empty native tab, verify its identity/font, then set names. Keep the captured current master explicitly in every symbol layerName. No Unicode lookup, slash parsing, missing-name filtering or master switch. Any build failure opens no tab. text: Menu actions and tool windows that are safe to remove under signal dispatch. What it does: OwnedMenus adds QActions to FontLab menus (or to one menu it owns) and shows widgets in tool windows. Each item gets an integer token. remove(token) and close() undo the items in a safe way. Why: A menu callback or a window button often removes its own item. If the host disconnects or deletes the QAction or QWidget while its signal still dispatches, PythonQt deletes the signal receiver twice and FontLab crashes (AGENTS.md: disconnect before deleteLater ; never tear down in a slot). Every slot that this class connects counts a dispatch depth. While the depth is above zero, remove and close queue their work. One shared zero-delay DeferredBatch timer runs the queue after the outermost slot returns. Each queued item runs once. How to use: menus = OwnedMenus(qt, fontlab, error_sink=sink) token = menus.add_action("Edit", "My action", callback) menus.remove(token) or menus.close() at unload. token, window = menus.tool_window(widget, "Title", on_close=done) . Rules: GUI thread only. qt is the PythonQt module and fontlab is the FontLab module; the caller passes both in. Callbacks take no arguments. Their errors go to error_sink(error, owner) and never reach Qt. QAction.text is a property in PythonQt, not a method. Guard scope: The dispatch guard covers only the slots that this class connects: menu triggered and the tool-window close. A signal that the caller connects itself (for example a button in the tool window) does not raise the depth. If such a slot calls remove or close , the teardown runs at once, inside that dispatch. Such a slot must queue its own call, for example with QTimer.singleShot(0, ...) . Subclasses wrap their own slots with _slot (Glyport's plugin host does this for Apply/Cancel). Cold import: stdlib plus fontlabapp.core.signals.deferred and fontlabapp.qt.safe .

text: Keep PythonQt widget pointers alive during native list conversion. What it does: qt_list converts a native QList of object pointers with cyclic GC off. main_window finds FontLab's main window with the same safety. Why: PythonQt wraps each pointer as a Python object. That allocation can start the cyclic collector, which can free a Python-owned widget that is still in the list. The next pointer then dangles and FontLab segfaults in PythonQtPrivate::wrapPtr (measured on FontLab 9.0.9780). Thread rule: GUI thread only, and the guard enforces it. gc.disable() is process wide. A call from another thread could re-enable collection while the GUI thread is still converting. The guard does not stop an explicit gc.collect() or reference-count destruction. Missing window: main_window raises MainWindowNotFound when FontLab has no main window. It is a RuntimeError with the old text, so older callers that catch RuntimeError or match "main window not found" keep working. New callers catch the class: the off-thread refusal stays a plain RuntimeError and is therefore never taken for a missing host. Cold import: stdlib only. Callers pass fontlab and qt in.

text: Paint over FontLab's glyph editor: one overlay per visible glyph window. What it does: EditorPainters lets a script register painter callbacks. FontLab calls each callback once per laid-out glyph, after the native glyph layer is painted. Each call gets a PaintContext with the glyph-to-canvas map, the canvas-to-view map and a ready QPainter . How to use: painters = EditorPainters(qt, fontlab, error_sink=sink) where qt is the PythonQt module and fontlab is the FontLab module. token = painters.register("after_native_layer", callback) starts the work. painters.remove(token) stops one painter. painters.close() stops all of them. After the last painter is gone, the poll timer stops and every overlay is detached. layer_filter is "active" (default), "inactive" or "all" . document_id limits a painter to one font ( package.id ). Inside the callback, draw with context.painter and map glyph units to pixels with context.glyph_to_canvas then context.canvas_to_view . Native facts (FontLab 9.0.9780, measured by Glyport; evidence glyport-ui/probe-editor-paint.json ): - The native canvas paints the viewport from an event filter and fills it opaquely. A Python pre-paint leaves no visible pixel. Only painting after the native layer works, so before_native_layer raises ValueError here. - A transparent child widget of the viewport paints after the native canvas. This module uses one such child per viewport. - A glyph unit maps to a pixel as the native glyph paint does: glyph transform, then text-block transform, to canvas units, then flCanvas.mapToViewportF to pixels. Kerning is already in the glyph transform. Why this design: - New glyph windows appear at any time. A 250 ms poll finds them. Hidden (closed) tabs stay alive, so only visible windows get an overlay. - Callback errors go to error_sink . Nothing raises out of paintEvent : an exception there, with a QPainter active, crashes FontLab (AGENTS.md landmines). - The painter is saved and restored around every callback. One plugin cannot leak pen, brush or transform state into the next. - Teardown disconnects each signal before deleteLater . A widget deleted with live Python slot targets crashes FontLab (double delete in PythonQtSignalReceiver ). - Maths come from fontlabapp.contours.affine . Native widget lists come through fontlabapp.qt.safe.qt_list (GC off during conversion). Compare fontlabapp.qt.painting.drawing.Drawing : that class paints one given widget. This module is a registry over all glyph windows. Glyport's fontlab_glyport.drawing.editor subclasses it. The subclass adds the Glyphs UnsupportedCapability refusal for the before-native phase and the layer_resolver wiring.

text: neighbours ( block : Any , index : int , info : Any , report : Callable [[ Exception ], object ]) -> tuple [ Side , Side ] Return (prev, next) beside paragraph glyph index ( info ). block.getPrevGlyphInLine / getNextGlyphInLine take the paragraph index and return None across a line break (a-stub; a-src fltextblock.cpp compares lineIndex ). Kerning is kerningOffset(True) / transform.m11() (a-src metrics tool): the layout value, classes applied, plus any drag offset, in font units; it is 0 when the block's kerningProcessing is off. A mirrored slot (negative m11 ) flips its sign. The pair (prev, this) is read from prev and (this, next) from info ; that side convention is (c), unverified natively. A missing or null neighbour glyph gives None. Each side fails alone: an unusable scale, a non-finite kerning or a failing lookup makes that side None and goes to report ; the other side is kept.

text: Shared metadata-safe glyph catalogue read for the studios (Scriptmix TODO:48). What: glyph_records(package) returns exactly what the three private copies in the Font Info tools (Calculate Vertical Metrics, Glyph Order Preview and Export, Unicode Ranges and Codepages) return: [(name, [code, ...])] in legacy FL.fl.font order, refused with the same message when the package is not the current one. catalogue(package) adds the per-glyph facts the Font Audit tabs read: per-master advance widths and contour counts, the current master's components, composite and mark/note/export flags. How: codes come from core.scripting.names_font_glyphs ( CurrentFont glyphs), never from flGlyph.fgGlyph ; the legacy names must list the same glyphs in the same order, otherwise the read is refused (no silent reorder). Layers are read with findLayer , components through shapeData ; no FontGate attribute is probed. Read-only and Qt-free. Used by fontlabapp.studios.font_audit ; A12/A29/A30 replace their copies with it.

text: The dry-run-then-Apply tab of Advance Widths (Round & scale, Tabular, Marks). What: LayerPanel shows the master scope of the originals' metrics panels, the tab's own controls and a GlyphTable of exactly the layers Apply changes (real glyph and master per row, skip notes kept). Refresh re-reads the selection, plans once and stores that snapshot; Apply writes exactly the shown pending layers through widths.apply (refused as stale when a layer changed in between). The "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" tick is off by default, shown only with a rebuild note, and resets whenever the planned glyph set changes. Used by the Advance Widths tab modules.

text: Round & scale tab: Round Advances and Scale Advances in one dry-run tab. Round: step 1 to 100 (default 10; Scriptmix TODO:76 adds step 1, steps 2 to 100 unchanged), Nearest/Up/Down, selected glyphs or every glyph; the advance changes, outlines and left sidebearings stay put. Scale: 10 % to 400 % (default 100 %) of the selected glyphs; the change is split between both sidebearings. Apply writes one Advance Widths: round advances … or … scale advances … Undo step.

text: Table tab: Width Table, read-only. One row per selected glyph: its advance in every master (font order) and the progression (rising, falling, flat or ⚠ mixed). "Show only mixed progressions" filters; "Select flagged" selects the mixed glyphs in the Font window. Nothing is written: no history, no font edit. As in the original, a selected glyph that no longer resolves refuses the read ("Selected glyph source changed; reopen this tool.") instead of being dropped, and "Select flagged" first re-reads the masters and the widths behind the shown rows, refusing (and clearing the table) when either has changed.

text: Tabular tab: Tabular Width (dry run, then one Undo step) and Check Tabular Widths (read-only). Tabular Width gives figures, figures and currency signs, or the selected glyphs one shared advance per master (the widest in the set, or a fixed 1 to 5000 units, default 500) and centres their ink. Apply writes one Advance Widths: set tabular width … Undo step. Check compares the exact advance of every selected layer occurrence with the first one ( fontlabapp.metrics.tabular_width.model.capture ); it never writes.

text: Advance Widths plans, dry-run snapshots and the one write path. Qt-free. What: the Scriptmix constants and planners of Round Advances, Scale Advances, Tabular Width and Zero-Width Marks (copied unchanged), the layer survey of fontlabapp.metrics.panel.model and apply : it writes exactly the entries a tab showed, refuses with "press Refresh" when a planned layer changed after the dry run, and commits every layer through one AppShell.history call labelled "Advance Widths: <action> <subject>" (Issue 235 §1.3/§1.4). shift_and_set moves the outline and sets the advance of each explicit layer, as the originals did. Used by the tabs of fontlabapp.studios.advance_widths .

text: Pure planners of Align & Nudge: align/distribute, interpolated nudge, overlap nodes, simplify. What: each planner reads a transform_studio.geometry.Layer snapshot and returns Change rows whose edit holds snapshot steps ( ("node", …) , ("shape", …) , ("remove", …) ), or a skip note string. Nothing here touches FontLab, so every rule is tested without the host. Why: behaviour parity with the Scriptmix Scripts/Contours tools Align And Distribute, Interpolated Nudge, Overlap Nodes and Simplify Selected Nodes, whose behaviour is restated in each function's docstring.

text: The four Align & Nudge tabs over the shared Transform Studio Tab scaffolding. What: Align & distribute (eight operations, selected geometry or all nodes, selection bounds or a typed coordinate), Interpolated nudge (x/y distances), Overlap nodes (italic angle of each written master) and Simplify (alternate selected nodes of the preview master, applied to the same structure on every chosen master). Each tab has a "Preview …" button that fills the table and draws the ghost without writing, and an apply button that writes one labelled step. A planner error (conflicting tips, mismatched structures) becomes a row problem, which refuses the whole write as the original scripts did. Why: one window replaces four Scriptmix Scripts/Contours tools (Phase D A24).

text: Anchor Studio maths: Qt-free planners, safety checks and the read-back check. What: A layer's anchors are read once into Pin tuples (name, x, y). Every planner turns those pins (plus the layer's ink box and advance) into Change rows; a Change with an edit is written, one with a problem is shown and refused. Edits are ("set", name, (x, y)) (add the anchor or move the only anchor of that name), ("remove", index) and ("rename", index, new) where index is the pin's place in the snapshot. verify compares the stored anchors with the planned result within TOLERANCE and names every sub-unit move that FontLab rounded to no change (Scriptmix TODO:78), so the studio reports it instead of claiming success. Why: The planners reproduce the Scriptmix Scripts/Anchors tools; keeping them free of Qt and FontLab makes every rule unit-testable. Used by fontlabapp.studios.anchor_studio.session and .tabs .
title: fontlabapp.studios.anchor_studio.model

text: Anchor Studio state: native layer reads, anchor plans and one-step writes. What: Studio keeps the glyph list, the preview master and the last plan. plan reads each named glyph's explicit layer on the chosen masters ( flGlyph.findLayer ; never fgGlyph ), snapshots its anchors into model.Facts and runs a planner. Missing, auto, empty-planner and hinted layers are skipped with a note. apply builds every native pin first, then writes all pending layers through AppShell.history as one "Anchor Studio: <action> <subject>" Undo step on those explicit layers, reads every layer back and checks it with model.verify : a move beyond model.TOLERANCE or a sub-unit move that FontLab rounded to no change is reported as "Partly applied", never as success (Scriptmix TODO:78). Why: Contract §1.3/§1.4. Hinted layers stay refused until the user runs "Remove PostScript hints", the shared Issue 241 remover ( fontui.remove_hints ). Read-only paths ( plan , census , cloud , rings , optical ) never open history. Used by fontlabapp.studios.anchor_studio.tabs .

text: The five Anchor Studio tabs: Place, Align, Rename & delete, Clean-up and Overlays. What: each tab is a plain Qt widget over the shared Studio state with the same glyph row (names field, "Use font selection", preview master and "All masters") and a sortable GlyphTable of the last plan or reading: one row per anchor change, or one row per skipped layer with its note. Choosing a row shows that glyph in the TGlyph preview (contract §1.8). Every writing action has a "Preview" button that plans without writing and an apply button that writes one labelled Undo step. The Overlays tab only reads. Why: one window replaces the eleven Scriptmix Scripts/Anchors tools (Phase D A3). Used by fontlabapp.studios.anchor_studio (tab builders and show ).

text: From components tab: Derive Anchors From Components as a dry run, then one Undo step. Recovers missing base anchors from positioned mark components over the whole current font and every master, with the original's rules (unchanged derived_points ): a scan failure shows in the tab and turns Apply off. Apply writes one Anchor Transfer: derive anchors <subject> Undo step.
title: fontlabapp.studios.anchor_transfer.components

text: CSV import tab: Add Anchors From File as a dry run, then one Undo step. Reads a UTF-8 CSV (path field, Browse… and Load, as the original; the original's columns, BOM and newline handling and its errors are unchanged in transfer.load_table ), lists the anchor edits on the current master and imports exactly those. Coordinates round half up to font units. Apply writes one Anchor Transfer: import anchors <subject> Undo step.

text: Between fonts tab: Copy Anchors Between Fonts as a dry run, then one Undo step in the destination. Every original choice, with its default: source and destination font and layer (or " All masters ", matched by name), "Copy from" all or selected glyphs, "Which anchors" all or a comma-separated list, "Location" absolute or relative (x scaled by the advance ratio), "Handle Collision" overwrite or rename (default), "Collision rename" incoming or destination (default), the "Addon suffix" (".bak") and "Use italic angle" with its angle (10°). Refresh captures both fonts and lists every edit anchors.crossfont.model.copy_layer plans; Copy writes them through the crossfont backend as one Anchor Transfer: copy anchors from <font> to <subject> Undo step in the destination font. The same font on both sides is refused. Two-font history and reopen are qualified natively in T29.

text: From glyph tab: Copy Anchors From Glyph as a dry run, then one Undo step. Copies the anchors of a named source glyph into the selected glyphs, master by master: "Add and move (keep other anchors)" or "Replace (remove anchors the source lacks)", x scaled by the advance-width ratio (on by default; both coordinates are rounded as the original reads them, then x becomes round(x * ratio) ), on the current master or all masters. The source glyph itself and layers that one side lacks are skipped. Apply writes one Anchor Transfer: copy anchors <subject> Undo step.

text: Between masters tab: Mirror Across Masters as a dry run, then one Undo step. Copies each selected glyph's anchors from one master ("From master", the current master by default) into the ticked masters ("To masters", every other master by default). "Scale x by advance-width ratio" is on and "Only add missing anchors" off, as in the original; positions round half up. Apply writes one Anchor Transfer: mirror anchors <subject> Undo step.

text: Anchor Transfer plans, dry-run snapshots and the write paths. Qt-free. What: the planners of Copy Anchors From Glyph ( anchors.copy.model.plan ), Mirror Across Masters, Derive Anchors From Components and Add Anchors From File (their pure functions copied unchanged from Scriptmix), the plan of anchors.writer.collect and apply : it re-plans from the live font, refuses with "press Refresh" when the plan or a target layer differs from the dry run, and writes exactly the shown edits through one AppShell.history call labelled "Anchor Transfer: <action> <subject>" (Issue 235 §1.3/§1.4). Coordinates are written as each original computed them; nothing is rounded again. Copy Anchors Between Fonts writes another font: fonts_preview plans it with anchors.crossfont.model.copy_layer and fonts_apply hands the same options to the crossfont backend, one Undo step in the destination font with this app's label. Used by the tabs of fontlabapp.studios.anchor_transfer .
